candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — combined oral contraceptive administration
candidate.educational_objective: Apply CDC guidance for one missed hormonally active combined oral contraceptive pill.

options.A: Take the missed pill as soon as possible and continue the remaining pills at the usual time.
options.B: Discard the missed pill and take only the next scheduled pill.
options.C: Discard the current pack and begin a completely new pack immediately.
options.D: Take two additional pills at the next scheduled time regardless of when the missed pill is remembered.

candidate.rationale: CDC U.S. Selected Practice Recommendations state that if one hormonally active combined oral contraceptive pill has been missed for 24 to less than 48 hours, the client should take the missed pill as soon as possible and continue the remaining pills at the usual time, even if this means taking two pills on the same day. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For one missed hormonally active combined oral contraceptive pill 24 to <48 hours late, take the missed pill as soon as possible and continue remaining pills at the usual time.
